batch_note: Yes. All 24 'finding, if true' items share one template: four sites laid out as a factor grid (hypothesis factor, rival factor, one shared confound such as slope, elevation, soil, rail, wealth, a wet/slump year or a fault), and the four options are always (1) the key, isolating the factor with the confound held fixed, (2) a comparison that crosses the confound, (3) a comparison that bears on the rival, and (4) a reversed or both-predict comparison. A student who learns 'eliminate any option that crosses the named shared confound, then any that only bears on the rival' gets most of them without weighing evidence. For weaken items the key is repeatedly the rival-only site beating the hypothesis-only site head to head (A-02, A-04, B-05, C-01, D-04), with the cleaner within-factor weakener present only in its supporting form. All 8 table items share a second template: two thresholds, the key is the only option that clears both, and the main trap clears one threshold narrowly (often the most extreme value); options print only part of the needed cells. Keys are spread across letters, so this is a structural tell, not a positional one.
